title: Stellar: Energy-Efficient and Low-Latency SNN Algorithm and Hardware Co-Design with Spatiotemporal Computation
problem: State-of-the-art SNN algorithms achieve high accuracy and sparsity but suffer from low energy efficiency and high latency due to complex neuron models. SNN hardware designs struggle to exploit data reuse and parallel processing due to irregular and time-dependent spike patterns.
motivation: Spiking neural networks have great potential to reduce energy consumption in AI applications compared to traditional artificial neural networks.
method: STELLAR proposes an algorithm-hardware co-design using Few Spikes (FS) neurons and few spikes backpropagation (FSBP) to train SNNs with short time windows and minimal spikes. A dedicated SNN architecture implements spatiotemporal Row Stationary (stRS) dataflow to exploit sparsity with parallel processing. Window-based parallel processing and spatiotemporal encoding-based computation architecture further enhance efficiency.
key_novelty: Algorithm-hardware co-design exploiting spatiotemporal dynamics through Few Spikes neurons paired with spatiotemporal Row Stationary dataflow for simultaneous energy efficiency and low latency.
contributions: Few spikes backpropagation (FSBP) training methodology with hardware awareness for efficient SNN training
Spatiotemporal Row Stationary (stRS) dataflow for exploiting sparsity in parallel SNN computation
Window-based parallel processing technique for rapid inference
primary_theme: Energy-efficient neuromorphic computing through algorithm-hardware co-design
